## Contract review

**Head reviewed:** `aa467bcf6bb405966e0172084f7ca3bd43f250bb` (branch `claude/issue-8913-object-kanban-columns-declared`, base `efead6c6054371d8c487e98395d44a7743ab7bbc`; `git merge-tree --write-tree` against `origin/main` `6112e0dad375fc37b6c1b1b79eedf033ba67c495` exits 0 — no conflict).

**Tier fuse (read, not self-described):** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER = 'claude-fable-5-1'` at `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:10505` on `objectstack-ai/objectstack` `origin/main` `331a1a2b09caf3ea89f3dacbbf8f8de717d3c1cc`. My own transcript (`subagents/agent-a46660e37d5cfc529.jsonl`, located by a marker string written to disk first) carries 151 harness `model` stamps at the final reading, every one `claude-fable-5-1`, no other value, no fallback notice. Reading = tier, so this verdict stands.

**How it was measured.** Fresh clone of objectui at the head, `pnpm install` rc 0, dependency closure of `plugin-kanban` plus `@object-ui/types` built rc 0. Every rc written to a file before any pipe; every mutation proved on disk (marker grep + blob hash) before its result was read, restored by `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`, `git diff HEAD` proved empty after each leg. Nothing was pushed, labelled, merged or approved. PR CI at this head: 34 check runs, all `success` (the two `skipped` are dependabot and the coverage shard).

### ① Derived judgments — the accept-set and public-face changes, named and judged

**Surface moved.** `ObjectKanbanSchema` gains `columns` on both faces: TS (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts:3029-3048`) and zod (`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:1261`, lane object `:1222-1229`). Element: a bare string, or a lane `{ id: string|number, title: string, cards?, limit?, className?, collapsed? }`. No new exported symbol (`ObjectKanbanLaneSchema` is module-private). `check-widening-tells` on the objectui board with `--declaration no` lists exactly the 7 T1 tells the seat recorded (6 lane keys + `columns`), and `check-clause2-carriers --pair 8989` exits **0** for me too.

**Direction — narrows only. VERIFIED, not accepted on the dev's word.** `BaseSchema` carries `[key: string]: any` (`packages/types/src/base.ts:492`) and its zod twin ends `.passthrough()` (`base.zod.ts:449`); `.extend` keeps that policy, so before this PR `columns` was admitted with any value and surfaced unexamined. The first `it` in the pin parses an undeclared key and asserts it validates AND survives into the parsed output — I ran it green at the head. Ablation (declaration deleted from the mirror; marker 1→0, blob `f521de02…`→`0a909b13…`): **11 failed / 21 passed** — all 10 REFUSES rows red, all 10 CONTROL rows green, the strip row red — identical to the dev's reading. So the control leg lights, the refusals are attributable to this declaration alone, and the accept set of the zod face is strictly a subset of the pre-PR set. **Correct.** (`Clause-②: yes` is still the right declaration: the tells are real new keys on a published validator; the label and the declaration agree.)

**Element shape vs the protocol.** Protocol at objectstack `eabdd66f` `component.zod.ts:2670-2671` (now `:2714-2715` at `331a1a2b`, byte-identical text): `columns: z.array(z.unknown()).optional()` with the union stated in `describe` prose — `{ id, title }` per `groupBy` value, or bare value strings. Shipped admits **both** prose arms (I ran the ACCEPT rows at the head: bare strings, `{ id, title }` with no `cards`, static lanes with cards). Where shipped is stricter than the protocol's *literal* `z.unknown()` it is on members the protocol does not name (`cards`, `limit`, `className`, `collapsed`) and on the value types of `id`/`title`; that judging is exactly what the ruled card asked to restore and it matches the renderer read set, which I recounted over every non-test file in `plugin-kanban/src`: `id` 31, `cards` 18, `title` 10, `limit` 10, `collapsed` 6, `className` 2, `color` 0, `items` 0 — six read, six declared. **Correct**, with two exceptions below (F1, F2).

**Card title falsified — REPRODUCED.** Zod leg (mirror rewritten to `z.array(KanbanColumnSchema)`, blob `f521de02…`→`5d3bc10e…`): **7 failed / 25 passed** — bare strings, the protocol's own `{ id, title }` example, the numeric id, the mixed array, the `items` strip row, and the two annotated TS-face boards. TS leg (TS face rewritten to `columns?: KanbanColumn[]`, blob `d3f2bfa9…`→`bda51de1…`): **13 `error TS`** (8× TS2741 `Property 'cards' is missing`, 5× TS2322 with the same nested cause) in five `plugin-kanban` board fixtures. `KanbanColumn` (`complex.ts:123-138`) and `KanbanColumnSchema` (`complex.zod.ts:131-139`) both require `cards`; the renderer reads `col.cards || []` on both bucketer legs (`index.tsx:62-64, 86-89`); the protocol's gate-validated example (`content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx:778-793`) authors three lanes with no `cards`. **The falsification holds.**

**Second premise falsified (`columns[].items`) — REPRODUCED.** `KanbanColumnSchema` is a plain `z.object` (strip posture), so on the retired arm `items` was accepted-and-dropped and the refusal came from required `cards`. With the declaration ablated, the strip row goes red (nothing strips when nothing declares) — i.e. before this PR `items` rode passthrough; after it, it is stripped. **Holds.**

**⭐ False green — REPRODUCED end to end.** With the TS face mutated and `dist` NOT rebuilt, `dist/objectql.d.ts` still carried the union (marker 1/0) and `tsc -p packages/plugin-kanban/tsconfig.test.json` exited **0 with 0 errors**. After `tsc -p packages/types/tsconfig.json` the marker flipped to 0/1 and the same command exited 2 with the 13 errors; after restore + rebuild, 1/0 and 0 errors again. The dev's re-run measured the change; `"paths": {}` in `tsconfig.test.json` is the mechanism, as reported.

**Strip posture and the `color` tombstone.** No in-repo non-test consumer renders or persists the mirror's parsed output: `SchemaRenderer.tsx:84-86` reads only `valid`/`errors` from the structural core validator, `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:59-78` prints only `type/id/label/children.length`. The strict twin (`StrictAnyComponentSchema`, walker `strict-authoring-face.ts:206-236`) recurses through object/union/array and I measured it refusing `columns[0].items` and accepting well-formed lanes — so the strip posture is a tolerant-face-only fact and no strict consumer is wired yet. `color` has zero read sites on this face and is taught nowhere for `object-kanban` (grep of the two doc pages and the plugin README). Both dispositions stand; no seam found.

**Pin — live subject or frozen defect?** The 10 REFUSES rows and their controls pin live subjects. **Two ACCEPT rows freeze defects:**

- **F1 — `id: number` blesses a shape the reader mis-buckets.** The PR body, docblock, changeset and both doc pages justify the number arm with "the renderer coerces with `String(col.id)`". That is true at exactly one site — the i18n lookup in `localizeColumn` (`ObjectKanban.tsx:956`) — and false at the site that decides lane membership: `bucketCardsIntoColumns` builds `knownIds` from raw `col.id` and compares it with `Object.keys(groups)`, which are strings (`index.tsx:100-103`). Measured by calling the real function with lanes `{ id: 1 }, { id: 2 }` and records `status: 1` / `status: '2'`: lanes read `1:r1`, `2:r2` **and** `__uncolumned__:r1+r2` — every card rendered twice, once in its lane and once in "Uncategorized". String-id control: `one:r1`, no duplicate. `ObjectKanban` reaches this function through `KanbanRenderer` with `...effectiveSchema` (`ObjectKanban.tsx:1299-1312`), so the object-kanban path is the affected one. The retired arm (`KanbanColumnSchema.id: z.string()`), the runtime type (`KanbanColumn.id: string`) and the protocol prose (no type named) give no backing for `number`; no fixture in the repo authors a numeric lane id (grep). The card's scope was to *restore* lane judging; on `id` the PR widened it past the arm being restored, on a misread of the renderer, and pinned the result ("a NUMERIC lane id — the renderer coerces with `String(col.id)`"). **Wrong.**
- **F2 — the mixed array has no reader.** `effectiveColumns` dispatches on `columns[0]` only (`ObjectKanban.tsx:964-976`): string-first → the whole array is ignored and lanes come from the picklist/data; object-first → every string element goes through the object branch. Measured on the bucketer with `[{ id: 'done', title: 'Done' }, 'todo']`: a blank lane with no `id`/`title` is emitted and the record with `status: 'todo'` lands in "Uncategorized". The protocol prose reads as two array shapes ("`{ id, title }` per `groupBy` value, **or** bare value strings"), not a per-element mix; the per-element union `z.array(z.union([...]))` admits a shape neither the protocol names nor the renderer handles, and the row "the two arms mix in one array, as a partially-labelled board authors them" pins it as admitted-whole with no corpus example cited. **Wrong.**

**F3 — docs teach an inert spelling silently.** `schema-reference.md` (new `columns` row and the objectui#8913 note) and `plugin-kanban.mdx:85-92, 106, 137` teach "a bare value string" as a valid `columns` element on `object-kanban` without saying that on this face — where `groupBy` is required — the renderer never honours it (`ObjectKanban.tsx:964-970` has no `return` when `groupBy` is set). The PR body and objectui#8990 record the unreachability; the published docs do not. Under the principle in force — quoted verbatim, untranslated: 「我们的项目以 objectstack 协议为准，文档应该以实际实现为准。协议不正确的应该先修改协议。」 — the docs must follow the actual implementation. The same pages also carry the F1 sentence ("`id` may be a number, because the renderer coerces it"), which is false as measured. **Wrong.**

Everything else derived from the diff is correct: `cards` optional with `KanbanCardSchema` as the one card authority (objectui#6939's `cardHasNoTitle` is refused again — I ran `kanban-column-cards-6939.test.tsx` green, 11 tests, vector `{ cardsIsAString: false, cardHasNoTitle: false, cardsAbsent: true, wellFormed: true }` with its inverted control), `limit`/`className`/`collapsed` typed as the boards read them, no new export, `zod-mirror-parity` untouched, `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` entry left accurate (it is `AWAITING_A_PIN_NEWLY_JUDGED` on the registry `inputs` ledger, a different obligation).

### ② Semver

Changeset: `'@object-ui/types': minor`. Precedent in this tree, not inferred: `.changeset/5903-objectgantt-declared-keys.md` and `6051-gantt-flat-config-declared-keys.md` declare previously-passthrough keys on a published face, state "a declared key is now type-validated, so `readOnly: 'yes'` is refused where it used to parse green — the same narrowing objectui#5074 landed", and are `minor`. The `patch` precedent for an accept-set shrink (`packages/types/CHANGELOG.md` 17.6.0, `ReportFieldSchema.type`) applies only to removing a spelling with no working renderer — not this shape. AGENTS.md §版本号策略 forbids `major` in the fixed group; `check:changeset-no-major` passes. **`minor` is the right level.** The changeset text, however, carries the F1 claim and must be corrected with it (it is the release-notes input).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 (clause-② declaration) — A, correct.** Seven real T1 tells against a `no` is C5; the dev's label was the honest reading and the seat's re-declaration to `yes` is what the diff says. I re-ran `--pair 8989`: rc 0. Not overturned.
- **Q2 (`color` tombstone) — A, correct.** Zero read sites, not taught for this face, and a by-name refusal on a different published face is a separate decision; recorded in the docblock. B stays a two-line follow-up if the tombstone owner wants it. Not overturned.
- **Q3 (strip posture) — A, correct.** No wired consumer reads the parsed output; the strict twin already closes lane keys where closing is wanted. Not overturned. One sentence worth adding somewhere: "accepted and dropped" is the tolerant face's posture; the strict twin refuses.
- **out_of_scope: objectui#8990 — correctly filed, and the arm decision is acceptable, but not silently.** `groupBy` is required on both objectui faces (`objectql.zod.ts:1256`) while the protocol has `z.string().optional()` — objectui narrower than the protocol on a published key, the direction the principle names; a relaxation is a widening that needs its own ruling. Refusing the bare-string arm here would be a *second* narrowing on a key the protocol names, which the dispatch forbade and the principle forbids — so admitting it for protocol parity is right. ⛔ **Do not block this PR on #8990**: the card is maintainer-ruled ("A now, C as the follow-up card"), #8990 is an unruled widening, and stacking a ruled card behind an unruled one inverts the order. The condition is F3: the docs and the pin file must say the arm is admitted for parity and inert on this face, with #8990 as the carrier.
- **out_of_scope: the false-green mechanism** — verified and generic; agree with "noted, not filed". **`object-kanban.dataSource`** — confirmed a component-level binding, not a member. **`MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS`** — agree, accurate as left. **`schema-reference.md` sentence** — verified corrected in the diff.

### Independence

```

Reviewed-by: session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w / subagent agent-a46660e37d5cfc529 (mode:subagent, harness model claude-fable-5-1)
```

**SELF-REVIEW.** Implementer and reviewer are subagents of the same dispatch session. Context isolation is not independence: the same seat's assumptions could be shared, so this record does not satisfy an independent-review requirement and is reported as a self-review. It does not soften the technical judgment above; every claim was re-derived from the tree and from the running code rather than from the implementer's report.
